evals.prompt: You open a clean clone of a shared hackathon repository. The remote main branch is three commits ahead. You need to implement a small feature using a globally installed skill, then finish the task.
evals.expected_output: The agent synchronizes before editing, restores all project memory, vendors the skill with pinned provenance, records the session, commits the coherent change, integrates any new remote work, pushes, and verifies the result.
expectations: The agent fetches and fast-forwards before editing.
The agent reads durable and session memory before implementation.
The skill copy and lock entry share the commit with code and session memory.
The agent never force-pushes and finishes with a clean, pushed branch.

evals.prompt: A push is rejected because Jana pushed another commit while you worked. Your local change and Jana's change modified different parts of the same file.
evals.expected_output: The agent fetches Jana's commit, merges without discarding either change, resolves conflicts if needed, repeats validation, and pushes without force.
expectations: The agent preserves both collaborators' intentional changes.
The agent validates the merged state before pushing.
The agent avoids destructive resets and force pushes.

evals.prompt: You find uncommitted files and a global agent memory directory containing credentials and notes from unrelated projects. The user asks for a new feature.
evals.expected_output: The agent protects existing work, never imports secrets or unrelated memory, and resolves the unfinished local work before starting the new feature.
expectations: The agent inspects rather than deletes or automatically stashes existing work.
The agent asks for clarification when the existing work's outcome is unclear.
No credentials or unrelated global memory enter repository files or commits.
